title: 4Sum
statement: Return every unique group of four values (from four different positions) that add up to the target. The same set of values must not appear twice; order does not matter.

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(18)
    return [[r.randint(-500, 500) for _ in range(300)], 0]

hints.1_question: Think of 4Sum as 'fix one number, then solve 3Sum', and 3Sum as 'fix one, then two pointers'. What do you need to do about duplicates at each level?
hints.2_nudge: Sort. Two nested loops choose the first two numbers; two pointers search for the remaining pair. Skip repeated values at the first two levels and after each match.
hints.3_big_hint: Skip i if nums[i] == nums[i-1]; skip j if j > i+1 and nums[j] == nums[j-1]. Then run l, r as in 3Sum, skipping duplicates of l after a match.

known_bugs.name: no duplicate handling
known_bugs.followup: If the array contains repeated values, can the same quadruplet be found more than once? Where do you prevent that?

known_bugs.name: skips j when it equals nums[j-1] even if j is the first choice after i
known_bugs.followup: For [2,2,2,2,2], when i = 0 and j = 1, nums[j] equals nums[j-1]. Is j really a duplicate choice there, or the first choice for its level?

known_bugs.name: tries every quadruple (O(n^4))
known_bugs.followup: How many nested loops do you have? Which innermost two can two pointers replace?

followups: How would you write a general kSum recursively?
What changes if values can be very large (overflow in other languages)?
